q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to an 8-month-old for fever — it is not to be used in children younger than 6 months, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is another option, given every 4 to 6 hours [6]. Do not give aspirin to a child unless their provider says it is OK [6].

Do not give ibuprofen if your child is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [2]. Do not alternate ibuprofen and acetaminophen unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [2].

Get medical advice if:
- Your child is not their usual self or is not eating [2]
- They show signs of dehydration, such as fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, or no tears when crying [2]
- The fever lasts 5 days or more [2]
- The medicine is not helping [3]

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Vomiting twice in a morning is often the start of a stomach bug, and the main risk is dehydration, according to the SEUP [1]. The most important thing is to keep fluids going in.

Wait 20 minutes after a vomit, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour [3]. If he keeps it down, you can slowly give it more often [3]. Do not use homemade drinks like lemonade or fizzy drinks [3]. You can buy oral rehydration solution for children without a prescription [5].

Get help if:
- He is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds [7]
- He vomits a lot, cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even when he has taken nothing [7]
- The vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [7]
- He is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or passes little urine [7]
- He has severe belly pain or a headache [7]

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [3].

What to do now: give oral rehydration fluids, which you can get over the counter [2]. After your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution, 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour [5]. If they keep it down, you can slowly increase how often you give it [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [5]. Sports drinks may help with mild dehydration but do not replace important nutrients and minerals [2].

Get help if:
- Your child is very drowsy or limp [3]
- They vomit many times or refuse all fluids [3]
- They vomit even when taking nothing [6]
- Vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [6]
- You think they are severely dehydrated [2]

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is common and often eases on its own, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Coughing is a reflex that clears the throat and airways, and it helps the body protect itself [6].

What can help now: give your child water to drink, or add moisture to the air with a steamy shower or a vaporizer — water can ease a cough either way [6]. Do not give cough medicine: children under four should not have it, and for children over four you should use caution and read labels carefully [6].

See a doctor if:
- The cough lasts longer than 2 to 3 weeks [6]
- Your child has a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice, or difficulty breathing [3]
- Your child is getting worse or not getting better [3]
- Coughing comes in bouts with a "whoop" sound, vomiting after coughing, or trouble breathing [2]

If your child has severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turns pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails, get medical help right away [4].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough comes in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound gasping between coughs, it may be whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, coughing bouts begin that can last several weeks or months [4].

Keep him comfortable and offer fluids often. Coughing fits can bring up thick mucus and make him vomit, so keep meals small if that happens [4].

Get medical help if:
- Coughing bouts last minutes, worse at night [4]
- A "whoop" sound between coughs [4]
- Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout [4]
- Turning blue or grey [4]
- Vomiting with the coughing [4]

For babies under 3 months, coughing may be absent and breathing may pause — get care right away [1].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with a child who is eating normally, is not itself a sign of anything serious in the passages here. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

Keep offering fluids and let him eat as he normally would; a poor appetite for a few days will not hurt him [3]. There is no need to treat a fever he does not have.

Get help if:
- He becomes drowsy and hard to wake [1]
- He has difficulty breathing — grunting, stomach sucking under the ribs, or breathing very fast [1]
- He is not responding like he normally does, or is not interested in feeding or normal activities [1]
- His skin, lips or tongue turn blue, grey or paler than usual [1]
- He has a stiff neck or a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it [1]

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
A rash of red spots that came on today is common in children, and most rashes can be cared for at home [5]. Raised, itchy spots or patches may be hives, which can usually be treated at home [5].

If the spots are itchy, bathe your child in cool water and pat the skin dry without rubbing, dress them in loose clothes, and ask a pharmacist about a cooling cream or gel or an antihistamine for the itching [1]. Give paracetamol for pain or discomfort, and do not give ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to [1].

Get help now if:
- swelling around the mouth [5]
- struggling to breathe [5]

See your doctor if the rash spreads, blisters, or your child seems unwell or distressed [6].

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
Itchy red bumps on a toddler's legs are often hives, which the NHS describes as raised, itchy patches or bumps that can appear anywhere on the body [1]. For a 2-year-old, a pharmacist can advise on antihistamine treatment to ease the itching, though this may not be suitable for young children [7].

To soothe the skin, keep it from getting dry and irritated, and avoid soaps, fabrics or lotions that seem to trigger it, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Try to stop him scratching, since scratching reddens the skin and makes the itch and swelling worse [4].

Get urgent help if:
- lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell [7]
- breathing is fast or struggling, or wheezing [7]
- throat feels tight or swallowing is hard [7]
- skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale [7]
- the child becomes limp, floppy or not responding normally [7]

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Spots that don't bother your child are often nappy rash, which is common in babies and can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. Nappy rash can look like red or raw patches on the bottom or the whole nappy area, or spots, pimples or blisters that may be red or brown [2].

Keep the nappy area clean and dry, change nappies often, and use a barrier cream at each change [2].

See your doctor if:
- the spots spread or get worse each day [2]
- the skin becomes scaly, dry or painful [2]
- your baby seems uncomfortable or distressed [2]
- the rash doesn't improve with home care [2]

If the spots are on the face, inside the elbows, behind the knees, hands or feet, and the skin is dry and itchy, this may be eczema, which is not contagious [5].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, but any symptom needs medical help, according to the NHS [2]. A bump on the head usually causes headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

For the headache you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [6]. Let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours, with no sport and no screens, then return gradually to normal activity [4]. He can eat normally and can sleep, though after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6].

Get help now if he:
- was knocked out or cannot stay awake [2]
- has a fit (seizure) [2]
- is vomiting repeatedly [4]
- is confused, or hard to wake [4]
- has trouble walking, speaking or seeing [2][4]
- has clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears [2][4]

Watch him over the first 24 hours for these signs [3].

text:
Vomiting once about an hour after a fall is one of the usual symptoms of a head knock, according to the SEUP [7]. A doctor should check any child who has vomited after a head injury, and the SEUP also says to go to the emergency department if the child is under three months, or if the fall was from more than one metre [1].

While you travel, keep the child with you and do not leave them alone. Do not give them anything to eat or drink if they are still vomiting.

Get help straight away if the child becomes drowsy or floppy, is confused or loses memory of the fall, has a headache that gets worse, vomits repeatedly or cannot keep fluids down, or has a fit [3][7].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are needed alongside it, according to the WHO [1]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the variety and texture of foods over time [1]. Aim for 2–3 meals a day at this age [1].

The NHS advises that how much your baby eats at first matters less than getting them used to eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2]. Offer a variety of foods alongside milk [2].

MedlinePlus suggests starting one food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting [5]. Do not give honey before age one, avoid cow's milk before age one, and avoid unpasteurised foods [5]. Cut up foods like grapes, and avoid sweets, popcorn and whole nuts because of choking risk [5].

Ask your health visitor or doctor when to start if your baby was born prematurely [2].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and it is offered on demand rather than in a set amount, according to the AEP [2]. If your baby has at least 4–5 breastfeeds a day, no other milk is needed [2]. Water comes with meals and is not measured: the AEP says babies should not be given added salt, and their kidneys are too immature to handle much of it [2]. During illness, the WHO says to increase fluids, including more frequent breastfeeding, and to offer soft, favourite foods [1].

When to get help:
- Refusing all fluids or feeds [1]
- Fewer wet nappies or dry mouth [1]
- Vomiting or diarrhoea that continues [1]
- Sleepy, floppy or hard to wake [1]

If you are worried about how much your baby is drinking, ask your doctor.
sources: [1] WHO — "Alimentación del lactante y del niño pequeño", section "Alimentación complement

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text:
It is common for babies and toddlers to prefer fruit and refuse vegetables, and the AEP says the taste for different flavours is built early: if you get the palate used to sour tastes like some fruits or bitter ones like some vegetables, they will eat more of them over their life [3].

Keep offering a wide variety of fruits and vegetables, at any daily meal, and vary how you present them — puréed, mashed, in small pieces [3]. Early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [3]. Offer whole fruit rather than juice: juice has no nutritional benefit over whole fruit, can lead to poor weight gain by displacing other foods, and increases the risk of tooth decay [3].

If your child is under one year, avoid green leafy vegetables high in nitrates, such as chard, spinach or borage, because of the risk of methaemoglobinaemia; if you do give them, they should be less than 20% of the plate [3]. Up to age 3, no more than one daily serving of these vegetables [3].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula alone is not enough: from 6 months on, solid foods should be introduced alongside milk, and they complement it rather than replace it, according to the AEP [2]. The WHO recommends breastfeeding continue up to 2 years or beyond while nutritionally adequate and safe complementary foods are introduced from 6 months [1].

What to do now: offer her solid foods in addition to her formula, not instead of it [2]. Aim for a varied diet with enough different foods and enough meals each day — most children this age worldwide do not get either [1]. If she is premature, the start of solids should be decided individually with her doctor [5].

When to get help: if she is not growing well, is losing weight, or you are finding it hard to get her to eat, speak to your doctor — poor nutrition in the first two years affects growth and development [3].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
It is normal for a newborn's pooping to vary a lot: the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one baby to another, and it is not essential that a baby poops every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is whether the stools are soft and the baby is comfortable, not a fixed number of times a day [6].

For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. If you are worried, your baby's doctor can check them.

Get help if your baby:
- Has hard, painful stools or blood in the stool [1][3]
- Has a lot of tummy pain or seems very unwell and is crying a lot [3]
- Is vomiting many times and cannot keep milk down [3]

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text:
It is common and normal for a 9-month-old to wake at night: night wakings are physiological, and nearly 30% of children still wake at night by one year, according to the PUC Chile manual [2]. The child should settle back to sleep on their own; if they always fall asleep in your arms, they will want the same conditions to fall asleep again [2].

What to do now: give them the chance to resettle by themselves rather than intervening, so a sleep habit is not created [2]. Keep a regular bedtime routine and avoid sleep deprivation, which makes night wakings more likely [3].

When to get help:
- Waking is accompanied by fever, which can trigger these episodes [1]
- The child seems unwell, feeds poorly, or is hard to wake
- Waking happens with snoring or pauses in breathing [5]
- It persists or you are worried about their growth or daytime behaviour [6]

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on only when he lies down is one of the signs of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus: coughing, especially at night or early morning, is a common symptom [4]. Other signs to look for are chest tightness, wheezing (a whistling sound when breathing out), shortness of breath, or getting tired easily [4].

What you can do at home, from the SEUP: offer fluids often, and for a small child you can do nasal washes with saline before sleep [5]. Keep him away from smoke and from places where people are smoking [5]. Do not use cough syrups, mucolytics or decongestants, especially in a child under 6 [5].

Get medical help right away if:
- Severe coughing or serious breathing problems [4]
- Turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [4]

If he has these symptoms, they need to be checked by your doctor.

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using albuterol more often than usual can be a sign the asthma is not fully controlled, and the SEUP says most flare-ups are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators, though symptoms can last up to a week [3]. Keep giving salbutamol with a spacer device — never straight into the mouth, as it works less well that way — and use a mask for small children [3][2]. If there is no clear improvement, the child needs to be seen at a health centre [3]. The SEUP lists these signs for going to the emergency department [7]:

- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale
- Breathing getting faster, ribs showing, chest or abdomen pulling in
- Needing inhalations every two hours or less

Avoid smoke and, during the flare-up, avoid exercise and allergens [3]. Children with repeated flare-ups should carry their inhaler to school [3].

q: my daughter is breathing faster after running but gets better when she rests
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Fast breathing that settles with rest is not one of the signs of breathing difficulty the SEUP lists for parents: those are ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, breathing fast at rest, or getting tired when walking or running [3]. A child who is well and has no fever can keep up their usual activity, according to the SEUP [3].

If your daughter is breathing fast only while running and it settles when she rests, that is the pattern the SEUP describes as normal activity tolerance, not the difficulty it asks you to watch for [3].

Get help if, at rest, she has:
- ribs pulling in or chest sinking [3][4]
- fast breathing or tiredness on walking or running [3]
- chest or side pain when breathing [4]
- a bad colour, or is limp, sleepy or very irritable [4]
- she refuses food and fluids [4]

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, an inflammation of the voice box and windpipe that often starts like a cold and causes a barking cough, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3].

Keep your child calm and comfortable, and offer fluids often. Croup is more common in children between six months and three years, and in autumn and winter [3].

Get help if:
- Breathing becomes difficult or you are worried about it [3]
- The ribs pull in or the chest sinks with each breath [1][2]
- Breathing is fast, or your child tires when walking or running [1]
- Your child becomes floppy, sleepy or very irritable [1][4]
- Chest pain when breathing [1][4]

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can have several causes, and one of them is asthma: chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply is a common symptom, according to the WHO [1]. Symptoms like this are often worse at night or during exercise, and can also be triggered by a cold, dust, smoke, pollen or strong smells [1]. Because symptoms like these can be caused by other conditions too, the WHO says anyone with them should talk to a healthcare provider [1].

Watch for these signs and get help if they appear:
- Difficulty breathing — ribs pulling in, chest sinking, breathing fast, tiring when walking or running [2]
- Chest pain when breathing [2][5]
- Looking unwell, drowsy, floppy or very irritable [2][5]
- Poor colour [5]
- Refusing food and fluids repeatedly [5]

If you are worried about your child's breathing, contact your doctor promptly [4].

text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [3]. Most febrile seizures do not need treatment [6].

If your child has another seizure: do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5]. Time the seizure.

Get help if your child:
- has a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes [2]
- has difficulty breathing [2]
- has stiffness and twitching on only 1 side of the body [2]
- is more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour after the seizure stops [2]
- has more than 1 seizure within 24 hours [2]

After a first febrile seizure, your child will need to be checked in hospital [6].

The HPV vaccine protects against human papillomavirus, a common virus spread through skin contact, usually during sex. Some types are linked to an increased risk of certain cancers, including cervical, mouth, anal, penile, vulval and vaginal cancer, and genital warts, according to the NHS [1]. It works very well at reducing the risk of getting HPV, and since it has been used there has been a big drop in conditions linked to HPV, such as cervical cancer and genital warts [2].

The ages at which it is offered follow the United States's national schedule, so ask your doctor when your daughter is due [1].

The most common side effects are mild and do not last long: swelling or pain where the injection was given, headache, high temperature, dizziness, feeling sick, tiredness [5]. A severe allergic reaction is very rare, and the person who vaccinates is trained to treat it immediately [5].

q: my son missed his 4 month vaccines, what do we do now

What to do now: contact your child's doctor or clinic and ask to book the missed doses as soon as possible. The exact ages and doses for your son follow the United States national schedule, so your doctor will tell you which vaccines are due now and how to catch up.

Get help promptly if your child has a fever, is breathing fast or with difficulty, is unusually sleepy or floppy, is not feeding well, or has a seizure [7].

q: my 11 year old needs a tetanus shot after a cut, does he need one
text:
Tetanus enters the body through cuts or wounds, and vaccination can prevent it, according to MedlinePlus [1]. DTaP is only for children younger than 7; older children and teens get different vaccines against tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis (Tdap and Td) [1].

Whether your son needs a shot now depends on his vaccination history and the wound, which a doctor has to assess. Tell the vaccination provider if he has had an allergic reaction after a previous dose of any tetanus, diphtheria or pertussis vaccine, or any severe, life-threatening allergies, or has ever had Guillain-Barré Syndrome [3]. Children with minor illnesses, such as a cold, may still be vaccinated [3].

After any tetanus-containing vaccine, soreness or swelling where the shot was given, fever, fussiness, feeling tired, loss of appetite and vomiting sometimes happen [3]. For signs that concern you, call your provider [3].

These symptoms last 3 to 5 days, then a rash of pinkish-red spots appears, starting on the chest, tummy and back before spreading to the face, neck and arms; it usually fades within 2 days [3].

Get help if:

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
Malaria is a potentially fatal disease spread by mosquito bites, and children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection, according to the WHO [1]. Early symptoms are often mild and hard to recognise as malaria: fever, headache and chills, usually appearing 10 to 15 days after an infected bite [2]. Because the symptoms are not specific, a test should be done as soon as possible [2].

Severe malaria can develop quickly — untreated P. falciparum malaria can become severe and cause death within 24 hours [2]. Get emergency care straight away for any of these:

- Extreme tiredness or fatigue [2]
- Confusion or reduced consciousness [2]
- Seizures (fits) [2]
- Difficulty breathing [2]
- Dark or bloody urine, yellow eyes or skin, or unusual bleeding [2]

Early treatment of mild malaria can stop the infection getting worse [2]. If your child has a fever after returning from Africa, have them tested for malaria without delay.

Get help today if:
- They fainted during exercise or while sitting [5]
- It came with palpitations or chest pain [5]
- They took more than 3–5 minutes to come round [5]
- There was shaking of the arms or legs, or they wet themselves [5]

If they feel faint again, sitting or lying down at once can stop it [6].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible in a living child — that number is almost certainly a misreading of the thermometer. Fever is a body temperature above normal, usually around 37 °C (98.6 °F), and it is not an illness itself: it is a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers in children come from infections, and some follow vaccines [1].

If the thermometer shows a high number, first check it is set to the right unit and take the temperature again — under the arm is fine, and a digital thermometer is best, according to the AEPap [5]. Fever rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F) and does not rise without limit [5].

What helps: take off extra clothing, offer fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath only if the child is comfortable [5]. If the child is uncomfortable, paracetamol or ibuprofen can be used — paracetamol is the first choice — and the dose depends on the child's weight [4]. Never give aspirin to a child with fever [1].

Get help if:
- The child is very drowsy, confused or irritable [6]
- Repeated vomiting or severe headache [6]
- A seizure (convulsion) [6]
- Breathing difficulty or unusual bleeding [2]

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is usually caused by a virus, like a cold or flu, and normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [4][5]. Tonsillitis is another common cause in teenagers, with red, swollen tonsils and problems swallowing [2].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes, ice lollies or hard sweets, and rest [5]. She can gargle with warm salty water — half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, then spit it out [5]. See a doctor if:
- She does not improve after a week [7]
- Very high temperature, or feeling hot, cold or shivery [7]
- Signs of dehydration, such as peeing less than usual [7]
- A lump in the mouth or neck, or a mouth ulcer lasting over 3 weeks [7]

Get help now if she has difficulty breathing, cannot swallow, or is drooling [7].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: the stool is hard and dry, and it can hurt to pass [3]. It usually lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

What helps, according to the SEUP: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool; add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit, vegetables; and don't replace fruit with juice, since juice has little fibre [1]. Keep to a regular routine and don't hold in the urge to go [1]. Laxatives or enemas should only be given if your paediatrician says so [1]. It's not essential that he poops every day — the rhythm and consistency vary from person to person [1].

- Severe tummy pain, or he is very down and complaining a lot [1]

- Vomiting many times, can't keep down solids or liquids [1]

text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are most often eczema, also called dermatitis, according to MedlinePlus [2]. It is not contagious, and scratching can make the redness, swelling and itch worse [2].

Keep the skin moist and avoid what irritates it: certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, stress, and things that cause allergy, such as some foods, pollen and animals [2]. Treatments can include medicines, skin creams, light therapy and good skin care [2].

- The itch is intense, especially at night [3]
- You see small bumps or lines on the fingers, wrists, arms or legs [3]

q: मेरे 2 साल के बच्चे को 39 बुखार है, पैरासिटामोल कितनी दूं?
text: बच्चे का वज़न कितना है? पैरासिटामोल की खुराक उम्र से नहीं, वज़न से तय होती है: वज़न बताइए, फिर सही मात्रा बताई जाएगी।

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर आंतों के संक्रमण का लक्षण है, और यह इलाज योग्य है [3][5]। WHO के अनुसार दस्त का इलाज ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) से किया जाना चाहिए — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है [3]। साथ ही ज़िंक की 10–14 दिन की खुराक दस्त की अवधि कम करती है और नतीजे बेहतर बनाती है [3]। ज़िंक की गोलियाँ दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% तक घटाती हैं [1]।

खाना न खाने पर: WHO कहता है कि दस्त के दौरान भी पोषक तत्वों से भरपूर खाना — जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है — देना जारी रखें, क्योंकि इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]।

मदद कब लें:
- दस्त लंबा चल रहा हो (14 दिन या ज़्यादा) [3]
- मल में खून हो [1]
- निर्जलीकरण के लक्षण दिखें [1]
- गंभीर निर्जलीकरण या शॉक हो तो नसों में तरल देना ज़रूरी है [1]

किसी स्वास्थ्यकर्मी से सलाह लें, खासकर लंबे समय तक चलने वाले दस्त, मल में खून या निर्जलीकरण के लक्षणों के लिए [1]।
sources: [1] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[3] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Overview", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/f
[5] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Key facts", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दानों के कई कारण हो सकते हैं। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं; दाने पहले चेहरे पर बालों की लाइन पर सपाट लाल चकत्तों के रूप में आते हैं, फिर गर्दन, धड़, हाथ-पैरों की ओर फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है, ऐसा CDC कहता है [4]। चेचक में मुख्य लक्षण खुजली वाले दाने हैं, जो शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दानों से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है [5]। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह के छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने आते हैं [3]।

दाने दिखें तो डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ, ताकि कारण पता चले। दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें।

मदद तुरंत लें अगर:
- मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो [6]
- बच्चा सुस्त हो या जवाब न दे

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।
sources: [3] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of hand, foot and mout
[4] CDC — "Measles Symptoms and Complications", section "3–5 days after symptoms begin: me
[5] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of chickenpox", p. 1 —
[6] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Raised, itchy spots or patches"

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है, वह अभी कीजिए। इस ख़ास स्थिति पर मेरे दिशानिर्देशों में और जानकारी नहीं है, इसलिए मैं ऐसा कुछ नहीं जोड़ूँगा जिससे आपको देर हो।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से जाँच करानी चाहिए, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [1]। अगर बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है या गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई है, तो भी तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [1]। डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि आगे कोई टेस्ट चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

रास्ते में बच्चे को होश में रखने की कोशिश करें और उल्टी होने पर उसे करवट पर लिटाएँ ताकि उल्टी गले में न फँसे। अगर बच्चा बेहोश हो जाए, बहुत नींद में लगे, बार-बार उल्टी करे, या उसका व्यवहार आम से अलग लगे, तो यह गंभीर हो सकता है — ऐसा SEUP बताता है [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज में मल त्याग करते समय बच्चे का रोना आम बात है, और कब्ज उन कारणों में से एक है जिनसे बच्चे रोते हैं [2]। कब्ज होने पर बच्चा पॉटी करते समय तनाव और दर्द महसूस कर सकता है, इसलिए वह रोता है।

अभी करने के लिए: बच्चे को आराम से बैठाएँ और शांत करें, और उसे पर्याप्त तरल दें। अगर बच्चा ठोस आहार लेता है तो फल और सब्जियाँ, और भरपूर पानी दें। अगर बच्चा केवल दूध पीता है तो उसकी मात्रा सामान्य रखें।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- रोना लगातार हो और शांत न हो [4]
- रोना सामान्य से अलग लगे [4]
- बुखार हो या दूध/खाना लेना बंद कर दे [4]
- मल में खून आए [6]
- पेट फूला, कड़ा हो या बच्चा सुस्त लगे [6]

अगर बच्चा बहुत कमजोर, बेजान लगे, साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो, या त्वचा नीली-पीली पड़ जाए तो तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [4]।
sources: [2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[4] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Crying and illness", p. 1 — https://ww
[6] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है, और खासकर हाथों-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा रंग दिख सकता है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। बुखार शरीर का बचाव है, अपने आप में गंभीरता की निशानी नहीं [4]।

अभी करें: बच्चे को ढेर सारे तरल पदार्थ पिलाएँ, ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। बुखार से परेशानी हो तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी दवा देने की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर है — PediBot के डोज़ कैलकुलेटर से पैरासिटामोल और आइबुप्रोफेन की सही मात्रा देख सकते हैं।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो या बना रहे [1]
- बच्चा सुस्त, बेहोश या भ्रमित लगे [6]
- उल्टी हो रही हो [6]
- तेज़ सिरदर्द हो [6]
- पेशाब कम आ रहा हो या मुँह सूखा लगे [1]
sources: [1] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html

[6] SEUP — "Golpe de calor. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿QUÉ ES UN GOLPE DE

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना निमोनिया की गंभीरता का संकेत है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेना चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को माँ की गोद में या खटिया पर लिटाए रखें और उसकी साँसों की गति पर ध्यान दें [3]। छह महीने से कम उम्र के शिशु में 60 से अधिक साँस प्रति मिनट, छह महीने से दो साल के बच्चे में 50 से अधिक, और दो साल से ऊपर के बच्चे में 40 से अधिक साँस प्रति मिनट तेज श्वसन माना जाता है [3]। बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]।

खतरे के लक्षण, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]:
- बुखार से दौरे पड़ना [2]
- खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से इनकार [2]
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना [2]
- सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज [2]
- त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक [2]
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio
[3] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलना ज़रूरी है [1]। तब तक बच्चे को मुँह से रिहाइड्रेशन घोल (ORS) छोटी-छोटी मात्रा में, बार-बार देना चाहिए [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर के पास जाना ज़रूरी है।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार आम बात है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [3]। त्वचा पर बैंगनी या ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर न मिटें, तुरंत ध्यान देने वाला लक्षण हैं [1][2]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [2]। 16 साल से छोटे बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। बुखार नापने के लिए डिजिटल थर्मामीटर बगल में रखें [3]।

मदद कब लें — इनमें से कोई भी दिखे तो तुरंत:
- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा [1]
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ [1]
- दाग जो दबाने पर न मिटें [1]
- कुछ भी खाना-पीना न ले पाए [1]
- 2 महीने से छोटा बच्चा या कमज़ोर रोग-प्रतिरोधक क्षमता [1]

दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, जो यहाँ उपलब्ध नहीं है — इसलिए कोई मात्रा नहीं बता सकती।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS CONSULTAR EN

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Paracetamol bukhar aur bechaini mein madad karta hai, aur aap ise 4 se 6 ghante ke antar par de sakte hain — din mein paanch baar se zyada nahi, AEPap ke mutabiq [3]. Dawa ki sahi matra bachche ke wazan se tay hoti hai, umar se nahi [3]; isliye apne bachche ka wazan dekh kar PediBot ke dose calculator se matra nikaal lein [3].

Agar aap paracetamol se shuru karte hain aur 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar tez hai aur bachcha bechain hai, to agle waqt ibuprofen dena theek hai [5]. Ibuprofen 6 se 8 ghante ke antar par diya jaata hai [3], lekin 3 mahine se chhote ya 5 kg se kam wazan wale bachche ko nahi dena chahiye [3]. Aspirin bachche ko na dein [2].

Doctor se milein agar:
- Bukhar 38-38.5°C se upar ho aur bachcha bechain lage [3]
- Lagataar ulti ho rahi ho [3]
- Bachche ko doray (convulsion) pad chuke hon [3]
- Wazan 3 kg se kam ho [3]

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona aam hai, khaas taur par sardi-zukaam ya asthma jaisi haalat mein [1][4]. Agar bachche ko sardi-zukaam hai, to koi ilaaj nahi hai, lekin kuch cheezein aaram deti hain: kaafi aaram, khoob saara taraL, saaf humidifier ya thanda vapouriser, aur saline naak ki boondein ya spray [6]. SEUP ke mutabiq khansi ke syrup, mucolytics ya cortisone faydemand nahi hain [2].

Doctor se milna chahiye agar:
- Saans lene mein takleef ya tez saans [6]
- Hothon ya chehre par neela rang [1][3]
- Seene ka dhadhakna ya seeti ki awaaz [1][3]
- Bukhaar 4 din se zyada [6]
- Lakshan 10 din se zyada bina sudhaar [6]

Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochein [6].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Mere bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli — yeh heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakta hai. NHS ke mutabik heat rash mein chhote, ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling, aur halki sujan hoti hai [4][6]. Yeh aam taur par kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6].

Ab kya karein: skin ko thanda rakhein taaki pasina na aaye aur rash na bade [4]. Dheele cotton kapde pehnayein, halki bedding use karein, thande paani se nahayein, aur dehydration se bachne ke liye khoob paani pilayein [4]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez — geela kapda ya ice pack (towel mein lipta hua) — 20 minute tak lagayein, aur rash ko kharochne ke bajaye thap-thap karein [4]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream na lagayein [4].

Doctor se milein agar: saans lene mein dikkat ho ya munh ke aas-paas sujan ho [5].

Bachche ko apne paas rakhein aur unhe akela na chhodein; agar wo sust ya soya hua lage to unhe hila kar jagte rahein [1]. q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kuchh bachche kabz ki wajah se potty karte waqt rote hain — yeh unka dard ya takleef batane ka tareeka hai [3]. Sabse pehle apne doctor ya health visitor se baat karein taaki kabz ki tasdeeq ho jaye aur sahi ilaaj mile [3].

Ghar par aap ye kar sakte hain:
- Bachche ko zyada paani ya doodh pilayein taaki potty naram rahe [3].
- Pet par halke haath se masaaj karein [3].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Bachcha lagatar ro raha hai aur chup nahi ho raha [7]
- Doodh peena band kar de ya kam kar de [7]
- Bukhar ho [7]
- 8 ghante se peshaab na aaye [7]
- Skin, hoth ya jeebh neeli, grey ya pale ho [7]

Yeh jaankari NHS se hai [3][7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, jaise bronchiolitis ya croup, jo aksar zukaam jaise halke lakshan se shuru hote hain [5][3]. Aise mein bachche ko shaant rakhein, seedha aur thoda utha kar rakhein, aur thoda-thoda kar ke doodh ya paani pilate rahein [5].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein zyada dikkat, seene mein gadgad ya pasliyan andar khinch rahi hon [5]
- Saans lene mein rukawat (pauses) [5]
- Hont, jeebh ya skin neeli ya grey ho jaye [5]
- Bachcha bahut sust ho, uth na raha ho [5]
- Doodh ya khana pehle se bahut kam le raha ho [5]

Agar bachcha 3 mahine se chhota hai aur bukhar 38°C ya zyada hai, ya 3 mahine se bada hai aur bukhar 39°C ya zyada hai, to turant doctor se milein [5].

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
Meri beti ki susti aur jag na paane ke baare mein: WHO ke mutabik, bachchon mein sepsis ke signs mein sust hona (lethargy) aur jag na paana (difficulty waking up) shaamil hain, aur aise lakshan dikhne par turant medical care leni chahiye [2]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki excessive drowsiness ya bachche ko jagane mein dikkat hona ek warning sign hai [3].

Agar aapko sepsis ka shak hai, to WHO kehta hai ki turant medical care lein [2]. Raaste mein, bachche ko aaram se rakhein aur unki saans par nazar rakhein; agar saans tez ho, skin pale ho, ya bachcha thanda lage, to yeh bhi sepsis ke signs hain [2].

Yeh signs dikhein to turant madad lein:
- Tez saans [2]
- Pale skin [2]
- Bachcha thanda lage [2]
- Dora (convulsions) [2]
- Kam peshaab ya peshaab na aana [2]

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं और छोटे बच्चों में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या आर.एस.वी. जैसी साँस की बीमारी का लक्षण हो सकता है, जिसमें साँस तेज़ चलती है और बच्चा ठीक से दूध या खाना नहीं ले पाता [3][2]।

अभी बच्चे को सीधा और आराम से रखें, बार-बार थोड़ा-थोड़ा दूध या पानी दें ताकि वह डिहाइड्रेट न हो, और नाक बह रही हो तो उसे साफ़ रखें [3][2]। मदद मिलने तक बच्चे को अकेला न छोड़ें और उसकी साँस पर नज़र रखें [3]।

इलाज के लिए जाने पर डॉक्टर को ये बातें बताएँ, क्योंकि ये ज़्यादा गंभीर होने के संकेत हैं:
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर धँसना या घरघराहट [3][6]
- साँस लेने में रुकावट या लंबे विराम [3]
- होंठ, जीभ या त्वचा का नीला या स्लेटी होना [3]
- बहुत सुस्त होना और जागने में कठिनाई [3]
- दूध या खाना बहुत कम लेना, या 12 घंटे से ज़्यादा सूखा नैपी [3]

अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है और उसका तापमान 38°C या ज़्यादा है, तो भी तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night and stops a 2-year-old sleeping is common with infections like whooping cough, which causes coughing bouts that are worse at night and can last several weeks, according to the NHS [2]. Croup also causes a barking cough that is often worse at night [5].

Keep the room cool and give small sips of fluid often. If the cough is dry, a warm drink may soothe it.

Get help if:
- The cough is very bad and getting worse [4]
- Lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [4]
- Breathing becomes hard or shallow [4]
- Chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- Seizures (fits) [4]

For a child under 5 with these symptoms, ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by more than one illness, and measles is one of them: it usually starts with fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes, and the rash begins on the face and neck and moves down over about three days, according to the WHO [4]. Chickenpox is another: an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and crusts, often starting on the face, chest and back, according to MedlinePlus [5].

There is no treatment for measles itself; the MMR vaccine prevents it [2]. For chickenpox, calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can ease the itching, and acetaminophen can help with fever — do not give aspirin, because with chickenpox it can cause Reye's syndrome [5].

Get help if your child has:
- Trouble breathing or severe respiratory problems [4]
- Confusion, seizures or unusual sleepiness [4]
- Severe diarrhoea or signs of dehydration [4]
- An ear infection [4]
- A rash that does not fade when pressed, or bleeding

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
A 6-year-old who has eaten nothing for 2 days needs to be checked, not reassured. Refusal to eat or drink is itself a warning sign, according to the SEUP [1].

What to do now: keep offering fluids and food rather than waiting for appetite to return. Give oral rehydration solution in small, frequent amounts — about 100–200 mL after each loose stool for a child over 2 years [6]. Keep offering their usual food in smaller, more frequent portions; there is no need to fast, and dairy can continue [7]. Avoid fizzy drinks, commercial fruit juices, tea and sports drinks [6][7].

Get help if:
- Refuses to eat or drink [1]
- Very thirsty, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or blood in the stool [1]
- Repeated vomiting, or vomit that is green, bloody or like coffee grounds [7]

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old can be a sign of bronchiolitis, an infection of the small airways that is most common in babies under 2 and usually starts like an ordinary cold with cough and mucus [6][5]. There is no medicine that cures it; most cases improve over about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [4].

While you are getting help: keep feeding them little and often, since feeding is harder when breathing is hard, and let them sleep propped up rather than flat [4]. Watch their breathing, how well they take their feeds, their colour and their general state [4].

Get help now if:
- Breathing gets faster or harder, or the ribs pull in [5]
- They struggle to feed or take less than usual [5]
- Their colour changes or they seem generally unwell [4]
- They feel floppy or you cannot wake them [2]

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में अपने आप उतर जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें [3]। निर्जलीकरण के संकेत देखें [3]। बच्चा खाना चाहे तो दें [3]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से जाँचते रहें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए ठीक है [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। बुखार में बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाइयों में न लपेटें [2]।

मदद कब लें:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [2]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [2]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]
- खाना न चाहे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [2]
- निर्जलीकरण — कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना [2]

अगर बच्चा सुस्त हो और जगाना मुश्किल हो, बहुत बेचैन या भ्रमित हो, साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, या सामान्य रूप से प्रतिक्रिया न दे — तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाएँ या स्पंज न करें — NHS के अनुसार बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, इसलिए बच्चे के कपड़े न उतारें और न ही उसे पानी से पोंछें [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए पैरासिटामोल दी जा सकती है, पर 2 महीने से छोटे बच्चे को नहीं [7]। आपके बच्चे का वज़न 5 किलो है, इसलिए आइबुप्रोफेन न दें — 3 महीने से छोटे या 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन नहीं देनी चाहिए [7]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है [7]।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [7]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [7]
- बच्चा खाना न चाहे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [7]
- पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना [7]

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।
sources: [7] NHS — "High temperature (fever) in children" (2025), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://w

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ (सिबिलेंस) ब्रोंकियल नलियों में रुकावट से होती है, और यह आमतौर पर सांस की वायरल बीमारियों के कारण होती है, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे लक्षण क्रूप में भी दिख सकते हैं, जिसमें भौंकने जैसी खांसी और सांस लेते समय तेज़, खुरदरी आवाज़ होती है, NHS के अनुसार [3]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को शांत रखें और सीधा बैठाएं, और अगर डॉक्टर ने सलबुटामोल जैसी ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवा दी है तो उसे दें — यह नलियों की रुकावट कम करती है [2]। दवा की खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए वही खुराक दें जो डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे पर लिखी हो [2]।

मदद कब लें:
- सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ या तेज़ सांस [3][6]
- खांसी के दौरे के साथ सांस लेते समय "हूप" जैसी आवाज़ [3]
- बच्चा दूध या खाना नहीं ले रहा [3]
- होंठ, चेहरा या नाखून नीले पड़ना [7]
- हालत बिगड़ती जाए या ठीक न हो [3]

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल, खुजली वाले छोटे दाने स्केबीज़ (खाज) के कारण हो सकते हैं — यह त्वचा में घुसने वाले सूक्ष्म कीड़ों से होता है, जिससे तेज़ खुजली और दाने निकलते हैं, और यह त्वचा के सीधे संपर्क से फैलता है [2]। स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही क्रीम या दवा से किया जा सकता है [4][2]।

इलाज शुरू करने के 24 घंटे तक दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें; 5 साल या उससे बड़े बच्चे इलाज शुरू होते ही स्कूल जा सकते हैं [1]। इलाज कीड़ों को जल्दी मार देता है, पर खुजली कुछ हफ़्ते तक बनी रह सकती है [1]। खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण (जैसे इम्पेटिगो) हो सकता है, इसलिए खुजाने से रोकें [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का शक हो [1]
- इलाज के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी हो [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों [1]
- घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है — सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं, और होने वाले दुष्प्रभाव मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं पर इनका मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]।

भारत में टीकाकरण की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती हैं — अपने बच्चे के टीके कब लगेंगे, यह अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता से पूछ लें [4]। टीके समय पर लगवाना सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा के लिए ज़रूरी है, और अगर कोई टीका छूट गया हो तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाया जा सकता है [4]।

टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं और जान बचा सकते हैं [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ke lakshan ho sakti hai: bachchon mein asthma se raat ko ya subah jaldi khansi hoti hai [5]. Agar khansi ke saath saans phoolna, tez saans chalna ya seeti jaisi awaaz ho, to yeh bhi isi taraf ishara karta hai [5].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa saaf rakhein aur bachche ko dhuen se door rakhein [7]. SEUP ke mutabiq agar broncoespasmo ho to salbutamol se ilaaj shuru kiya jata hai, aur inhaler hamesha spacer ke saath lagayein, seedha munh mein nahi [7]. Koi bhi dawa dene se pehle apne doctor se poochhein [4].

Doctor se turant milein agar:
- Bachcha bahut bechain ya sust ho, ya chehra aur honth neele ya pale ho jayein [7]
- Saans lene mein takleef badhe: tez saans, pasliyan saaf dikhein, pet zyada chale ya seene mein gadhaapan ho [7]
- Inhaler har do ghante ya usse zyada baar chahiye ho [7]
- Khansi ke saath saans phoolne ki shikayat ho [5]

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Agar bachche ko sirf halki chot lagi hai, to zyadatar bachche jaldi theek ho jate hain, lekin pehle 24 ghante dhyan se nazar rakhna zaroori hai [4]. SEUP ke mutabik sar ki chot ke baad aaram karna chahiye [3].

Ab kya karein: agar dard ho to paracetamol ya ibuprofen apne doctor ke bataye hue dose mein de sakte hain [6]. Bachcha so sakta hai, lekin zyada gehri chot mein use har 4 ghante mein jagana chahiye [6]. Khane-peene mein koi khaas badlav ki zaroorat nahi, apni aadat ke hisaab se doodh ya khana de sakte hain [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Baar-baar ulti [3]
- Tez ya badhta sar dard [3]
- Bechaini ya jagane par na uthna [3]
- Baat ya chalne mein dikkat [3]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani [3]

Agar bachcha 3 mahine se chhota ho ya girne ki unchai 1 meter se zyada ho to bhi turant dikhayein [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein badan par laal daane kai alag-alag kaaranon se ho sakte hain, aur zyada tar maamle viral sankraman se hote hain, MedlinePlus ke mutabiq [1][6]. Daane khujli wale, laal, dard bhare ho sakte hain, aur kuch mein chhaale ya kachi skin ke dhabbe bhi ban sakte hain [1].

Ghar par aaram karein, khujli ke liye moisturizer ya lotion laga sakte hain, aur zaroorat par antihistamine dawa se khujli kam hoti hai [1]. Agar daane kisi cheez ke chhune se hue hain to us cheez se door rakhein [1].

Doctor se milein agar:
- Daane bahut zyada ya gambhir hain [1]
- Daane theek nahi ho rahe [1]
- Saath mein doosre lakshan bhi hain [1]

Khaas taur par agar bukhar, khaansi, naak behna, aankhon mein laal-pan ya munh ke andar safed daane hain, to ye khasoosan khatarnak ho sakta hai [3][5].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: polio (VPI) ke teeke rashtriya vaccination calendar ka hissa hain, jo 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein diye jaate hain, aur 6 saal ki umar par booster bhi [3]. WHO ke mutabik difteria ke teeke aksar polio ke teeke ke saath milakar diye jaate hain, aur teeke lagwana bimariyon se bachne ka sabse asardar tareeqa hai [6].

Agar aapke bachche ki koi dose chhoot gayi hai, to apne doctor se milein taaki pending dose jaldi lag jaye [1].

Kab doctor se milna hai:
- Teeke ke baad bachcha theek na lage ya saans lene mein dikkat ho [1]
- Teeke ki jagah par sujan ya bukhar jo kam na ho [1]

Agar aapke bachche ko koi teeka lagane se pehle koi bimari hai, to doctor ko batayein [1].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea is usually a symptom of an infection in the digestive tract, and it can be caused by many different bacteria, viruses and parasites, according to the WHO [6]. It is treated with oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [1][4]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Give ORS in small amounts, and keep feeding as usual [1][4]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार, डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का इंजेक्शन लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव सामान्य हैं — चिंता की बात नहीं [5]। खसरे के टीके में इंजेक्शन के 6-7 दिन बाद हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं; इनका इलाज ज़रूरी नहीं, ये अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

इंजेक्शन के एक-दो घंटे बाद पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक के बारे में इंजेक्शन देने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें — खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है [5]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- लक्षण 2-3 दिन में ठीक न हों [5]
- इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए [5]

टीकों की उम्र भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when the body cannot cool itself, usually after too long in the sun or heat, according to the SEUP [1]. Dizziness is one of its symptoms [1].

What to do now: move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to help lower their temperature [6]. Do not give fever medicines for heat illness — use physical cooling measures instead, according to the AEPap [5].

Get help if:
- Fever above 39°C that does not come down with home measures [7]
- Loss of consciousness or seizures [7]
- Confusion, trouble speaking or moving [7]
- Persistent vomiting, cannot keep fluids down [7]

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text:
Solid khana, jise weaning ya complementary feeding bhi kehte hain, tab shuru karna chahiye jab bachcha taqreeban 6 mahine ka ho, NHS ke mutabiq [2]. Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke bachcha kitna khata hai — ahem yeh hai ke woh khane ki aadat ho jaye; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh ya first infant formula se milte hain [2].

6 mahine tak sirf doodh dena behtar hai kyunke is se bachcha bimariyon aur infections se mehfooz rehta hai, aur itne waqt mein woh khana nigalne ke qabil ho jata hai [4]. Doodh ke saath saath alag alag qism ke khane dene se bachche ki sehatmand khane ki aadat banti hai [2].

Shuru mein bachche ko seedha baithne ki halat mein high chair par rakhein, safety harness lagayein, aur 6 mahine se cup se pani ke chhote ghoont dein [6]. Agar bachcha waqt se pehle paida hua ho, to solid khana shuru karne ke waqt ke bare mein apne doctor ya local health worker se poochein [2].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Loose stools in a child are usually gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [2]. The most important thing is to prevent dehydration by giving oral rehydration solution, which you can buy ready-prepared without a prescription [3][6]. Give it in small amounts often, and keep offering it while your child has loose stools [3]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses [3]. Keep feeding your child, including breast milk if you are breastfeeding, and offer nutritious food [1]. Do not give medicine to stop the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your doctor [3].

Get help if:

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana

At 6 months, start with finger foods that break up easily in the mouth and are long enough for your baby to grip — pieces about the size of your own finger work well [5]. Avoid hard foods such as whole nuts or raw carrots and apples, to reduce the risk of choking [5].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text:
Malaria and teething are not told apart by the fever alone: the first symptoms of malaria are often mild and similar to many illnesses with fever, so it can be hard to recognise, according to the WHO [1]. The most common early symptoms are fever, headache and chills [1]. Malaria is a life-threatening disease spread by mosquito bites, mostly in tropical countries, and it does not pass from person to person [1].

If your child has a fever and you are in, or have travelled to, an area where malaria is common, get them seen and tested the same day — malaria is preventable and curable, and treatment stops mild cases getting worse [1]. Do not wait to see whether it is teething.

Get help straight away if your child has:
- fatigue or confusion [1]
- seizures [1]
- difficulty breathing [1]

Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: At around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are introduced alongside it, according to the WHO [3]. Keep breast milk or first infant formula as the main drink, and offer sips of water from an open or free-flow cup with meals [1]. Aim for 2 to 3 meals a day at this age [3]. q: how do I know if my child is dehydrated from diarrhoea
text:
Signs of dehydration include being very thirsty, crying without tears, passing little urine, or sunken eyes, according to the SEUP [2]. Marked irritability, drowsiness, or reduced responsiveness are also signs [2]. The risk of dehydration is greater the younger the child [2].

Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — in small amounts, and keep offering them [1][2]. Zinc supplements shorten the diarrhoea by about 25% and reduce stool volume by 30%, according to the WHO [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses [2].

Get help if:
- Very thirsty, no tears, little urine, sunken eyes [2]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness, or reduced responsiveness [2]
- Cannot drink as fast as they lose fluid [2]
- Refusing to eat or drink [2]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or a lot of blood in the stool [2]

Keep him resting physically and mentally for 24 to 48 hours — no sport and no screens — then return to normal activities gradually [4]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6].

- Intense or worsening headache, or one that does not improve with the usual medicine [4]

- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [4]

q: when to start feeding puree to 6 months old

Once you have started, move your baby on from puréed foods to mashed, lumpy or finger foods as soon as they can manage them. The most important thing is that your baby eats a wide variety of food and gets all the nutrients they need [1].

Give it at the dose recommended by your paediatrician, every 6 to 8 hours [2]. The aim is to make your child comfortable, not to bring the temperature itself down [2]. Make sure they drink plenty of fluids, keep the room at a neutral temperature and well ventilated, and avoid over-wrapping them so they can lose heat [2]. Do not bathe them in cold water or put wet cloths on them — it is unpleasant and does not work [2]. It is normal for them not to want to eat; do not force them, but keep offering fluids [2].

Get help if:
- Your child seems very unwell or is getting worse [2]
- They are not drinking or have fewer wet nappies [2]
- The fever lasts more than a few days [2]

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text:
Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts (ORS) to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements as a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and the stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [3].

Se venden en España:

q: le ha salido un sarpullido rojo por las piernas y le pica
text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica en las piernas puede ser una urticaria: son ronchas o habones rojos y elevados que pican mucho, y en la infancia la mayoría están causadas por una infección, según la SEUP [3]. También puede tratarse de una reacción a picaduras de insectos, que da lesiones que pican intensamente y aparecen sobre todo en brazos y piernas, según Ecimed [6].

Mientras tanto:
- Evita que se rasque: el rascado puede enrojecer más la piel y aumentar la hinchazón y el picor [1], y en las picaduras el rascado frecuente puede infectar las lesiones [6].
- No le pongas cremas ni lociones que le irriten la piel [1].

Busca ayuda si:
- Le cuesta respirar o tragar [3].
- Se le hinchan la cara, la lengua o los labios [5].
- Las lesiones se infectan (supuran o se ponen muy rojas) [6].
- Aparecen ampollas o el sarpullido se extiende o empeora [6].

Si el picor no cede o el sarpullido dura semanas, consulta a tu doctor [6].

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis es la inflamación de la capa externa del ojo y del interior del párpado, y puede causar hinchazón, picor, escozor, legañas y enrojecimiento, según MedlinePlus [4]. En la mayoría de los casos se cura sin tratamiento médico, aunque la conjuntivitis bacteriana necesita gotas o pomada de antibiótico [4]. Los ojos llorosos son frecuentes y a menudo mejoran solos [1].

Para las legañas pegadas al despertar, limpia los párpados con agua tibia; si hay infección, las gotas de antibiótico pueden ayudar, según el NHS [2].

Consulta a tu médico si:
- Tiene menos de 30 días y los ojos están rojos y pegajosos [3]
- Hay dolor en los ojos [3]
- Sensibilidad a la luz [3]
- Cambios en la visión [3]
- Ojos muy rojos [3]

Si los síntomas no se han resuelto en 7 días, también conviene consultar [3].

q: mi niño tiene fiebre y las manos muy frias, es normal?
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Manos y pies fríos en un niño con fiebre: puede ser mala circulación, hay que verlo
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre es la respuesta natural del cuerpo para combatir infecciones, según MedlinePlus [4]. Las manos frías pueden ser una señal de que la circulación no va bien, y el NHS pide atención inmediata cuando un niño con fiebre tiene las manos y los pies inusualmente fríos [2].

Mientras lo llevan a valorar: ofrézcanle líquidos con frecuencia y sigan dándole el pecho si es lactante [7]. No lo desabriguen ni lo bañen con agua fría para bajarle la temperatura, y no lo cubran con demasiada ropa ni mantas [2]. Pueden darle paracetamol o ibuprofeno si está incómodo o molesto, comprobando antes en el prospecto que sea adecuado para él [7]; la dosis depende de su edad y su peso, así que consúltenla con su médico o farmacéutico.

Busquen ayuda urgente si además tiene:
- Cuello rígido [2]
- Manchas que no desaparecen al presionarlas [2]
- Le molesta la luz [2]
- Está somnoliento y cuesta despertarlo [2]
- Respira con dificultad o muy rápido [2]

q: se le marcan las costillas al respirar pero luego se pone a jugar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado); Dificultad para respirar: respira rápido, «pitido» al respirar, se marcan las costillas
text:
Las costillas marcadas al respirar son un signo de dificultad respiratoria, según la SEUP [2][4]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño incorporado y tranquilo, y no le des nada por la boca si le cuesta respirar [4].

Señales que indican que va a peor:
- Está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable [2][4].
- Respira cada vez más deprisa o se le hunde el pecho [2][5].
- Mueve mucho el abdomen con cada respiración [4][5].
- Tiene mal color o se pone pálido o azulado [4][5].
- Rechaza la alimentación y los líquidos [4].

Que luego se ponga a jugar no descarta que la respiración esté costando: la dificultad puede notarse sobre todo al esfuerzo, y en ese momento hay que consultar [2][5].

q: no hay quien despierte a mi hijo y respira muy raro
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: No responde a estímulos; Dificultad para respirar: respira rápido, «pitido» al respirar, se marcan las costillas
text:
No hay que esperar a nada más: si no responde y respira mal, hay que actuar ya. Según la SEUP, ante un niño somnoliento o con problemas para despertarlo, o con dificultad respiratoria, hay que consultar en un servicio de urgencias [3]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño acompañado y no le dejes solo en ningún momento.

Estos son los signos que indican gravedad y que ya estáis viendo:
- No responde o cuesta mucho despertarle [3].
- Respira muy deprisa, se le marcan las costillas o se le hunde el pecho [2].
- Se pone morado o pálido [2].
- Está muy agitado o somnoliento [2].

Si tiene las vías respiratorias despejadas y no hay riesgo de que se ahogue con vómito, no le pongas nada en la boca. Llama al número de emergencias mientras lo vigilas de cerca.

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre y rigidez en el cuello
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Rigidez de nuca: hay que descartar una meningitis ahora mismo
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

La meningitis es la inflamación del tejido que rodea el cerebro y la médula espinal, según MedlinePlus [7]. Puede agravarse muy rápido, y la fiebre súbita junto con la rigidez en el cuello son señales para buscar atención médica de inmediato [7]. El tratamiento temprano ayuda a prevenir problemas graves [7].

Mientras consiguen ayuda, no le den nada de comer ni de beber si está muy decaído o somnoliento, y manténganlo acompañado y vigilado en todo momento.

Estas son las señales que indican que la cosa es más seria, según MedlinePlus [7]:
- Fiebre súbita y alta
- Dolor de cabeza fuerte
- Rigidez en el cuello
- Náuseas o vómitos

En el hospital harán análisis de sangre, pruebas de imágenes y una punción espinal para examinar el líquido cefalorraquídeo [7]. Los antibióticos tratan la meningitis bacteriana y los antivirales ayudan en algunos tipos de meningitis viral [7].
sources: [7] MedlinePlus — "Meningitis", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/meningitis.html

q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Caída por las escaleras o de más de un metro, o llanto que no se calma tras un golpe: que lo vea un médico hoy
text:
Tu hija tiene un golpe en la cabeza, que suele ocurrir por una caída, según la SEUP [1]. Los síntomas más habituales son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia [1].

Mientras la llevan a que la vean hoy, no le des nada de comer ni de beber si está somnolienta o confusa, y no la dejes sola. Si hay sangrado por la nariz o los oídos, no tapones el oído ni la nariz.

Señales que deben hacer buscar ayuda de inmediato, según MedlinePlus [4]:
- Dolor de cabeza que empeora o no mejora
- Vómitos o náuseas repetidas
- Convulsiones
- No puede levantarse
- Pupilas dilatadas, dificultad para hablar, debilidad o falta de coordinación
- Confusión, inquietud o agitación crecientes

La SEUP recomienda consultar en urgencias si la caída fue desde más de un metro de altura [3].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre despues de vacunarse ayer
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de vacunarse es un efecto esperado y pasajero. Según el CAV-AEP, tras la vacunación el niño debe estar monitorizado, y en prematuros puede aparecer de forma transitoria un empeoramiento leve, aunque estas situaciones son poco frecuentes [1]. El calendario de vacunación que se sigue en España es el del Ministerio de Sanidad [2].

Qué hacer ahora: ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia y ropa ligera, y déjalo descansar. No puedo darte una dosis: depende de la edad y el peso, que no conozco.

Consulta a tu médico si:
- La fiebre es alta o no baja con las medidas habituales.
- El niño está decaído, irritable o no responde bien.
- Aparecen manchas en la piel, vómitos repetidos o dificultad para respirar.
- La fiebre dura más de lo esperado o empeora en vez de mejorar.

Si el niño es prematuro o tiene alguna condición de riesgo, coméntalo con su pediatra [1].

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi hijo tiene 5 años y pesa 12 kilos, es normal?
text:
Según los patrones de crecimiento de la OMS (niño, 5 años):
• Peso para la edad: 12 kg → percentil 0.1 (z −3.22), bajo peso grave (por debajo de −3 DE).
⚠️ El peso está muy por debajo de lo que la OMS espera para esta talla o edad. Consulta con un médico pronto.
Dime también la talla y calculo el peso para la talla.
Un solo dato dice poco: lo que importa es la curva a lo largo del tiempo, y esa la tiene tu pediatra.

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
La erupción de los dientes de leche empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, según el manual de pediatría de la PUC de Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le haya salido ninguno puede entrar dentro de lo normal, porque la secuencia y el momento de aparición varían de un niño a otro [6].

Mientras tanto, puedes revisarle la boca con calma: mira los labios, la mucosa de las mejillas, las encías y la lengua, y aprovecha para empezar los cuidados de higiene oral [6].

Consulta a tu doctor si te preocupa que no le salga ningún diente, si ves las encías inflamadas o con heridas, o si notas problemas al masticar o al hablar [6].

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text:
Cuando un niño deja de decir palabras que antes decía, conviene hablar con su médico y pedir una evaluación del desarrollo, según los CDC [3]. Los CDC recomiendan actuar pronto: no esperar si el niño ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía [3].

Qué hacer ahora:
- Apunta las palabras que decía y cuándo dejó de usarlas, para contárselo al médico [3].
- Pide en la consulta una revisión del desarrollo; la Academia Americana de Pediatría recomienda hacer cribados con herramientas validadas cuando hay una preocupación de los padres [3].
- Si sigue habiendo dudas, pide que lo derive a un especialista que valore mejor a tu hija [3].

Según MedlinePlus, cuanto antes se empiezan los servicios de desarrollo (logopedia, fisioterapia), mejor es el resultado [5].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text:
El dolor de pecho después de hacer deporte suele deberse a una distensión o sobrecarga muscular: aparece tras el esfuerzo, puede empeorar al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo, según el NHS [1]. También puede ser ansiedad, que cursa con presión o dolor en el pecho, latido rápido y respiración acelerada, según la SEUP [3].

Lo que ayuda ahora: que descanse y pare la actividad; el dolor muscular mejora al reposar [1]. Si está preocupado, consulte a su médico, aunque la mayoría de los dolores de pecho no se deben al corazón [1].

Busque ayuda médica urgente si:
- El dolor no se va, o es opresivo o como ardor [7].
- El dolor se extiende al brazo, cuello, mandíbula, estómago o espalda [7].
- Hay sudoración, náuseas, mareo o falta de aire [7].

Consulte también a su médico si el dolor va y viene, o si se va rápido pero sigue preocupado [7].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. Después de un rato de reposo, los niños suelen recuperarse rápido, en un par de minutos [5].

Si vuelve a sentirse mal, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato, y que respire despacio y profundo [5]. Si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado para que respire mejor [5]. Cuando el malestar desaparezca, que se incorpore despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5]. Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio [4].

Consulta si:
- Tarda más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento [3].
- El desmayo ocurre haciendo ejercicio o esfuerzo [3].
- Hubo palpitaciones, dolor en el pecho o sacudidas [3].

q: mi bebe esta vomitando y no consigue quedarse con ni siquiera pequeños sorbos
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Vomita TODO lo que toma y no retiene nada: es signo de peligro, hay que verlo hoy
text:
Según la SEUP, si el niño vomita mucho y no tolera líquidos, hay que consultar de nuevo en urgencias [4]. Mientras tanto, ofrécele suero de rehidratación oral ya preparado, en pequeñas cantidades y con frecuencia, sin usar soluciones caseras ni refrescos [5]. Si toma pecho, mantén la lactancia normal o incluso más a menudo si lo pide [4]. No le des medicamentos para los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [5].

Señales para consultar:
- Vomita aunque no tome nada, o los vómitos son verdosos, con sangre o como posos de café [4].
- Mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco u ojos hundidos [5].
- Irritabilidad marcada, somnolencia o menos respuesta [5].
- Rechazo a comer o beber [5].
- Dolor abdominal persistente o intenso [5].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text:
La fruta y la verdura se pueden empezar a ofrecer en torno a los 6 meses, cuando la leche ya no cubre por sí sola las necesidades del bebé, según la OMS [2]. La AEP recomienda ir introduciendo toda la variedad disponible, en cualquiera de las comidas, variando también la forma de presentarla: triturada, chafada o en trozos pequeños [1]. No hay frutas mejores que otras para comenzar; la elección depende de los gustos de la familia [1]. Conviene ofrecer los alimentos de uno en uno, con intervalos de unos días, para ver cómo los tolera y los acepta, y sin añadir sal, azúcar ni edulcorantes [4]. Es mejor la fruta entera que el zumo: el zumo no aporta ventajas frente a la fruta y su consumo elevado puede favorecer el sobrepeso o las caries [1].

Durante el primer año, evita las verduras de hoja verde ricas en nitratos (acelga, espinaca, borraja) [1].
